Software Requirements Specification
Need Line wise MRP Approval same as Existing MRL Approval Functionality.
# 349251
Version 1.0●01 Sep 2025

###### Table of Contents
Purpose 3
Business Requirement 3
Assumptions 3
Functional Requirements 4

# Section 1: Overview

# Purpose
The purpose of this functionality is to establish a controlled, transparent, and auditable Material Requirements Planning (MRP) approval process within the ERP or production management system.

# Business Requirement
These requirements ensure that the MRP approval process is controlled, efficient, and auditable, aligning with procurement and production planning goals.
• All material lines go through proper approval workflows before procurement.
• Rejected or held lines are handled systematically with visibility on their impact on the BOM.
• The system supports incremental updates, minimizing rework and re-approval of unchanged items.
• Clear segregation of responsibilities and traceability for approvals, rejections, and holds.
• Improved accuracy in indent generation and material planning through structured validations and controls.
• A user-friendly UI with expandable views and checkbox selections, enabling efficient decision-making.

# Section 3.

# Functional Requirements
Need Line wise MRP Approval same as Existing MRL Approval Functionality.
• Need a new Approval permission in user group. I.e., MRP.
• It will be multi-level approval.
• We also need to handle the multi-level approval from the Multi-Level Approval Settings only.
Menu From pending MRP LIST
When user click on Run MRP in the BOM then system will open up the screen of Material planning screen to validate the all necessary details. Before sending it to the approval screen, the user must first review and validate the material details in the screen below. Once all necessary information has been confirmed, they will run the MRP.
Once will sent the approval request from the system will drive us on material requirement planning screen where we can club the multiple OC and run the MRP.
After this, we need to route it to the MRP-level screen, where only two levels of data should be displayed: the parent article and the child article (BOM). On this screen, the user should be able to take an action by creating either a production demand or a purchase demand.
Additionally, we are also providing the facility where user can also send the approval request from the Indent and User Indent List. This will be work based on the MRP approval permission is enabled.
Once this action is completed, the system will display the approval popup and automatically load the user list according to the approver configured as a default. If only a single user is associated with the approver, the system will automatically select that user.
We also need to introduce the column of sent to in the MRP activity log where we need to show the user name where we sent the approval of it.
• Whenever an approval is defined, the MRP will be routed for approval whenever the user attempts to run it.

• New BOM Line Identification: -
• Description: When a new line is added to the BOM and the MRP is regenerated, the newly added lines should be displayed with a white background.
• Purpose: This visual cue helps users easily identify which lines have been newly introduced in the BOM.
• Reference: As illustrated in the provided screenshot.
• Modified BOM Line Identification: -
• Description: - If a user modifies an existing BOM line and regenerates the MRP.
• The modified line should be highlighted with an orange strip.
• The updated value should be shown in orange.
• The previous value should be displayed on hover via the information icon (i).
• Purpose: This allows users to quickly recognize changes and compare current vs. previous values for audit and validation purposes.
• Unchanged BOM Line Identification: -
• Description: If no changes are made to a BOM line during MRP regeneration, the line should be displayed with a grey Strip.
• Purpose: This helps users easily identify lines that remain unchanged, reducing confusion and improving review efficiency.
• Deletion & Reject BOM Line Identification: -
• Description: If the line is deleted from the BOM then then, the line should be displayed with a Red Strip.
• Purpose: This helps users easily identify lines that remain unchanged, reducing confusion and improving review efficiency.
• Notification & Alert : Needs to handle in following screens: -
Need to handle this on Approval Pending, Approval pending with Others and Approved Today as well.
• We also need to handle following setting: -
Case: -
The table shows two different configuration options and how they influence the final required quantity (Req) used for MRL generation.
A. Exclude Extra Production % in MRL Generation
• OC Qty: 1200
• Calculated Req qty: 1320
• Note: Production % should NOT be considered, so the planned (PD) quantity must remain 1300.
B. Exclude Additional Production Quantities in MRL Generation
• OC Qty: 1100
• Calculated Req qty: 1210
• Note: Additional quantity should NOT be considered, but again, the PD quantity should be 1300.
Summary
The key point being demonstrated:
• Regardless of whether Extra Production % or Additional Quantity is excluded in MRL generation,
the PD (planned) quantity should still be calculated as 1300, matching the Total OC Qty derived from the Sales Order.
The table shows how different exclusion settings alter the intermediate required quantities, but the final PD quantity should remain consistent.
15. Introducing the MRP Approval Re-Assignment Feature
To handle situations where an assigned approver is unavailable, we are introducing a Re-Assign MRP Approval functionality.
Scenario Overview
Assume that the approval workflow for user A is configured with two possible approvers: X and Y.
• User A submits an MRP approval request.
• The system routes the request to Approver X as per the configured sequence.
• If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
New Solution: Re-Assign Approval
To avoid such delays, we are introducing a provision that allows the approval request to be reassigned from one approver to another.
Re-Assignment Options
Option 1: Re-Assign from “Approval Pending with Others”
• When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A.
• From there, User A will have the ability to re-assign the pending request from X to Y.
• This allows the originator (A) to redirect the approval to the next available approver.
Option 2: Re-Assign from “Approval Pending” by the Approver
• If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen.
• User X will have an option to re-assign the approval request to Y.
• This supports approver-level delegation.
Benefit
This feature ensures that:
• Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability.
• The approval process remains flexible and efficient.
• Both the requester (A) and the approver (X) have the authority to re-route approval to the next eligible approver (Y).
Note: - This log should be updated in the MRP Log.
Screenshot attached for the reference: -
Validation: -
• System should not allow to take the action on those OC in MRP pending list those are already in a waiting status. For this we need to add a new column also in the list with name Status where system will show the status of the MRP.
• BOM will be in disable mode on MRP waiting in approval status.
• System will show the value in required qty un-rounding for next level.
Note: -
• Checkbox selections should be retained at the OC (Order Confirmation) level only.
• If there is a new MRL generated for a different OC, the system should not retain checkbox selections from the previous OC’s MRL.

### Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process
This case study revolves around a Bill of Materials (BOM) in an MRP (Material Requirements Planning) system and its approval workflow. The scenario describes how the system handles rejections, approvals, line adjustments, and updates throughout the MRP process.
Here’s a detailed breakdown of each stage: -

#### Step 1: Adding Materials to the BOM
• Initially, 6 material lines are added to the BOM.
• Once the materials are defined, an MRP (Material Requirements Plan) is generated. This plan reflects the materials required for production based on the BOM.
• After generating the MRP, it is sent for approval.

#### Step 2: Rejection of Lines from MRP Approval
• The MRP approval board reviews the plan, but 5-6 lines are rejected.
• In the system, rejected lines are displayed with a red line against their respective material lines (lines 5 and 6).

#### Step 3: Regenerating the MRP and Sending for Approval
• After rejection, the MRP is regenerated for all 6 lines, meaning that the material lines (5-6) are now part of the new plan.
• The system now defaults with checkboxes for all lines (including the rejected ones). By default, lines 5-6 are checked.

#### Step 4: Unticking Line 5 and Rejecting Again
• Line 5 is unticked by the user (indicating that it’s no longer part of the approval request).
• Line 5 is then rejected.
• In the BOM, the system shows a red line against line 6 only, since line 5 was explicitly removed (unticked) and rejected, while line 6 remains rejected.

#### Step 5: Regenerating MRP and Sending for Approval
• The user regenerates the MRP and sends it for approval again.
• Upon resending, the system automatically ticks lines 5-6 by default, which means they are still considered in the plan for approval.

#### Step 6: Rejecting Line 5-6 Again
• The user rejects both lines (5 and 6) again from the MRP approval dashboard.
• As a result, the system shows red lines against lines 5-6, reflecting that both lines have been rejected again.

#### Step 7: Marking Line 4 as Awaited
• The user marks line 4 as "awaited" (perhaps pending further details, approval, or additional checks).
• When the MRP approval is sent, the system now showing the checkbox in line 4 because it is awaited.
• The system shows checkboxes for all other lines except line 4, while lines 5-6 are still default ticked.
• Awaited lines are typically excluded from the approval process, but the checkbox for the line is still shown as unticked.

#### Step 8: Marking Line 4 as "Ready For process"
• After further processing, line 4 is marked as "Ready for process" (indicating it’s now ready for approval).
• The user then resends the MRP for approval.
• The system now ticks all checkboxes, including line 4, and lines 5-6 remain default ticked.
• All lines are included in the approval process, and the system assumes they are ready to be processed for approval.

#### Step 9: Approving All Lines
• The user proceeds to tick all checkboxes and approves all the lines via the MRP approval dashboard.
• After approval, the system generates indents for all material lines. These indents are requests for the materials to be purchased or prepared for production based on the approved BOM.

#### Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)
• After the indents are generated and the cost sheet is revised, the user adds a new material (line 7) to the BOM.
• The user regenerates the MRP to include the new material.
• Upon sending for approval again, the system only shows line 7 (the new material) in the approval request.
• This suggests that the system recognizes the new line (line 7) as the only change to the MRP after the last approval cycle, and it requires separate approval for the new material.

### Key Observations & System Behavior
• Rejections and Red Lines: Rejected lines are indicated with a red line in the BOM, making it easy to identify which lines have been disapproved by the MRP approval board.
• Default Checkbox Behaviour: The system automatically ticks lines that are part of the MRP plan for approval (even rejected ones). Lines that are rejected or marked as awaited are unticked or displayed differently in the approval workflow.
• Awaited Lines Handling: When lines are marked as "awaited," they are excluded from the approval process (checkbox is unticked). Once they are unawaited, they are considered for approval, and their checkbox is ticked.
• Incremental Changes: When new materials are added (line 7), only the newly added line appears for approval, implying that the system tracks incremental changes and doesn’t resubmit the entire BOM for approval unless changes are made to multiple lines.
• Indent Generation: Once approval is given, the system generates indents for all lines, which are essentially action requests for procurement or production.
• Cost Sheet Revision: A revision to the cost sheet can trigger updates to the MRP and require a new approval cycle.

### Conclusion
The MRP system facilitates the approval workflow by allowing users to manage individual lines in the BOM, reject materials, mark lines as awaited, and approve changes incrementally. It ensures transparency by displaying red lines for rejected items, and it supports efficient approval and indent generation processes by focusing on only the modified lines when new changes are introduced.
This structured approval and material planning process helps maintain accuracy in the procurement and production cycles, especially when dealing with multiple materials and frequent updates.

- definition (§ Functional Requirements): To handle situations where an assigned approver is unavailable, we are introducing a Re-Assign MRP Approval functionality.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements): Assume that the approval workflow for user A is configured with two possible approvers: X and Y.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements): If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements): If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements): Functional Requirements: / 1. User A submits an MRP approval request. / 2. The system routes the request to Approver X as per the configured sequence. / 3. If Approver X is unavailable (e.g., out of office, on leave, or unable to respond), the approval cannot proceed, which may cause delays for urgent requirements.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements): When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements): Functional Requirements: / 1. When the request is pending with X, it will appear in the “Approval Pending with Others” section for User A. / 2. From there, User A will have the ability to re-assign the pending request from X to Y. / 3. This allows the originator (A) to redirect the approval to the next available approver.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements): If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements): Functional Requirements: / 1. If X is available but chooses to delegate, the re-assignment can also be done directly from the “Approval Pending” screen. / 2. User X will have an option to re-assign the approval request to Y. / 3. This supports approver-level delegation.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements): Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements): Functional Requirements: / 1. Urgent MRP approvals are not delayed due to approver unavailability. / 2. The approval process remains flexible and efficient. / 3. Both the requester (A) and the approver (X) have the authority to re-route approval to the next eligible approver (Y).

After further processing, line 4 is marked as "Ready for process" (indicating it’s now ready for approval). / 2. The user then resends the MRP for approval. / 3. The system now ticks all checkboxes, including line 4, and lines 5-6 remain default ticked. / 4. All lines are included in the approval process, and the system assumes they are ready to be processed for approval.

- dependency (§ Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)): This suggests that the system recognizes the new line (line 7) as the only change to the MRP after the last approval cycle, and it requires separate approval for the new material.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements › … › Case Study: MRP Approval and BOM Line Management Process › Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7)): Step 10: Adding a New Material (Line 7): / 1. After the indents are generated and the cost sheet is revised, the user adds a new material (line 7) to the BOM. / 2. The user regenerates the MRP to include the new material. / 3. Upon sending for approval again, the system only shows line 7 (the new material) in the approval request. / 4. This suggests that the system recognizes the new line (line 7) as the only change to the MRP after the last approval cycle, and it requires separate approval for the new material.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior): Lines that are rejected or marked as awaited are unticked or displayed differently in the approval workflow.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior): Once they are unawaited, they are considered for approval, and their checkbox is ticked.
- dependency (§ Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior): Cost Sheet Revision: A revision to the cost sheet can trigger updates to the MRP and require a new approval cycle.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements › … › Key Observations & System Behavior): Key Observations & System Behavior: / 1. Rejections and Red Lines: Rejected lines are indicated with a red line in the BOM, making it easy to identify which lines have been disapproved by the MRP approval board. / 2. Default Checkbox Behaviour: The system automatically ticks lines that are part of the MRP plan for approval (even rejected ones). Lines that are rejected or marked as awaited are unticked or displayed differently in the approval workflow. / 3. Awaited Lines Handling: When lines are marked as "awaited," they are excluded from the approval process (checkbox is unticked). Once they are unawaited, they are considered for approval, and their checkbox is ticked. / 4. Incremental Changes: When new materials are added (line 7), only the newly added line appears for approval, implying that the system tracks incremental changes and doesn’t resubmit the entire BOM for approval unless changes are made to multiple lines. / 5. Indent Generation: Once approval is given, the system generates indents for all lines, which are essentially action requests for procurement or production. / 6. Cost Sheet Revision: A revision to the cost sheet can trigger updates to the MRP and require a new approval cycle.
